card.name: The word male after female contexts
card.fires_on: The word "male" (and nearby spots) when male patients or partners are named right after a mention of women or female patients, mostly in pregnancy and reproductive warnings.

modes.label: Male partners/patients
modes.description: "male" naming male patients or partners in a contraception or pregnancy warning that has just discussed females.
modes.example: Patients must avoid pregnancy (female patients or female partners of<< male>> patients) while taking PEGASYS

modes.label: Stray punctuation or text near men
modes.description: Commas, brackets or numbers in passages about husbands, men or boys, where the word being predicted would be male-related.
modes.example: Richard implicitly draws a comparison between himself and Anne's dead husband<<,>> the murdered Prince Edward

card.writes: It pushes against male-related words like boys, brothers and guy, and toward female words, so the model leans away from male terms.
card.plain: It fires on the word male in warnings that pair female patients with male partners, and on a few other spots in male-focused text.
